In Pickens County in 1970, of 13,581 year-round housing units, 173 units were for sale, and 473 were for rent (Source: County-City Data Book, Appendix C). The 100 new families which the Applicant estimates would relocate in the project vicinity would most likely disperse over the area wherever housing is available.
Discussion with an Oconee County school official indicates that the county school system could absorb the influx of school age children of 100 new families, assuming that they all locate in Oconee County. Since it is more likely that the new families would disperse over both counties, the impact of additional school age children on the school system would be minor.
3.1.3.1 Recreation
Development of the proposed hiking trail and related features should have only a minor economic impact on the local area. Construction activities would be minimal and public use at any one time limited to a few individuals or small groups.
Existing local commercial service establishments should not benefit to any measurable extent. Expenditures for local public services, such as for police protection, hospitals, and highway maintenance, would not be significantly affected by the proposed recreation plan. Although there would be an increased potential for forest fires resulting from public use activities, proper recreation management policies could significantly reduce the risks involved. The Applicant would close the trail when hazardous conditions develop.
The social impact of the proposed recreation development would be beneficial in that those individuals interested in recreational activities associated with a primitive hiking trail would be afforded a new opportunity to participate in such leisure activities and thereby improve their physical and mental well-being.
